sections.content: How many people stayed in Braintree after gaining qualifications?

Braintree is a medium-sized town in the East of England. Braintree does not have its own university.

Braintree has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Braintree ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,900 state-school pupils from Braintree who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 420 (22%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 665 (35%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Braintree to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Braintree's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Braintree in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Braintree move to?

Of Braintree's graduates, 190 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 40 of those graduates (21%) were living fairly locally, in the Chelmsford travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Braintree's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 195 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 85 of those qualified non-graduates (44%) were living fairly locally, in the Chelmsford travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Braintree's GCSE cohort:

  • 120 graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 50 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East of England

In 2018 to 2019, 39% of graduates and 36% of qualified non-graduates living in Braintree had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 355 graduates and 725 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Braintree. This is compared with the 420 graduates and 665 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 61% of the graduates had also lived in Braintree as GCSE pupils, while 39% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Braintree in 2018 to 2019, 64% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 36% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
